title: WHY DO WE FORGET?
nextLesson: HOW DOES YOUR BRAIN CONTROL YOUR EMOTIONS?

o: Turning information into a form the brain can store
questions.good: Correct! Encoding is how information is first processed into a memory.
questions.hint: Think about what happens when your brain first receives information.
questions.review: Encoding, the first stage of making a memory.

questions.q: Which part of the brain is especially important for forming new memories?
questions.good: Exactly! The hippocampus helps form many new memories.
questions.hint: It sits deep inside the brain and links the parts of an experience.
questions.review: The hippocampus and how it forms new memories.

o: A small workspace that holds information for a short time
A process that only happens in sleep
The ability to remember every experience
questions.good: Correct! Working memory holds information while you use it.
questions.hint: Think of holding a phone number long enough to type it.
questions.review: Working memory and its small capacity.

o: The brain switching off in sleep
Connections between neurons becoming stronger or weaker with experience
questions.good: Well done! The brain adapts through experience.
questions.hint: Think about how practice changes the connections between neurons.
questions.review: Synaptic plasticity, how practice changes the brain.

o: Forgetting a new experience at once
The process that settles and stabilizes a new memory
questions.good: Correct! Consolidation makes new memories more stable.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a memory after it is first formed.

questions.good: Exactly! Sleep supports the settling of memories.
questions.hint: The brain stays active while you sleep.

o: When other memories make a memory harder to learn or recall
questions.good: Correct! Similar memories can compete with each other.
questions.hint: Think about mixing up an old and a new password.

o: Getting information back out of memory
questions.good: Well done! Retrieval is how you bring a memory back.
questions.hint: It happens when you try to remember an answer.
questions.review: Retrieval, and why it sometimes fails.

o: A machine that records brain activity
A hint, like a smell or song, that helps you find a memory
questions.good: Correct! A smell, a song or a photograph can bring a memory back.
questions.hint: Think about what can remind you of an old event.

o: Every memory is a perfect recording
Feeling confident proves a memory is correct
Remembering rebuilds the event, so details can change
questions.q: Which statement about memory is true?
questions.good: Excellent! Memory is rebuilt each time, so details can change.
questions.hint: Think about why two people can remember the same event differently.

o: Practising recall again and again over several days
questions.q: Which habit helps you remember for a long time?
questions.good: Excellent! Recall practice spread over time helps memory last.
questions.hint: Try to remember without looking at your notes.
